mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate over three consecutive months signals a tightening monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, which leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises by >25 bps in 3 months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of triggered episodes, or the average rank IC over triggered windows is below 0.10.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% indicates weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the mechanism fails when unemployment is simultaneously falling.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly unemployment rate (UNRATE) falling below 3.5% for two consecutive months signals an overheating labor market, which historically precedes both wage inflation and tighter Fed policy, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 55% of triggered episodes, or the mechanism fails during periods of falling inflation.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of more than 0.5% over three consecutive months signals weakening manufacturing activity, which reduces earnings for cyclically-sensitive sectors and results in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the mechanism fails when energy prices are simultaneously rising sharply.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both the unemployment rate (UNRATE) and payroll employment (PAYEMS) month-over-month is a contradictory signal indicating labor market choppiness; this ambiguity typically precedes elevated market volatility and negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE rises while PAYEMS also rises in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the mechanism fails during periods of stable inflation.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent decline in both real personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) and housing starts (HOUST) by more than 1% month-over-month signals a broad-based collapse in household demand, which depresses earnings and triggers negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 and HOUST both fall > -1% in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are positive in more than 45% of triggered episodes, or the mechanism fails when monetary policy is simultaneously easing.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly inflation rate (CPIAUCSL) above 3% for six consecutive months, coupled with a federal funds rate below 2%, signals a delayed monetary policy response; this typically leads to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days as markets anticipate eventual easing.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL > 3% for 6 consecutive months AND FEDFUNDS < 2%
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are negative in more than 55% of triggered episodes, or the mechanism fails when inflation expectations rise sharply.

mechanism_narrative: An always-on positive relationship exists between real personal income (proxied by RSAFS growth) and S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days; higher household income supports consumer spending and corporate profits, driving positive equity returns.
failure_condition: The correlation between RSAFS growth and subsequent 20-day S&P 500 returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.10) in out-of-sample tests.
